## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Water Movement

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.

The satellites’ changing separation is measured and used to infer shifts in mass. Scientists use those inferred shifts to investigate changes in water stored underground and in lakes and rivers, as well as in soil moisture, glaciers, and ice sheets. They also investigate sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.

The satellites do not directly measure groundwater. Instead, changes in their separation provide a measurement scientists use to infer shifts in mass associated with water movement.
